competitors.name: Di Fara Pizza
competitors.action: Di Fara launched a frozen Grandma-style pizza line in three SKUs (Classic, Vodka, Pepperoni), positioning it as the first Grandma-style frozen pizza in retail. The product is rolling out first at ShopRite and The Giant Company across NY, NJ, PA, and select CT/MD stores at a $12.99 price point, with national expansion planned for the second half of 2026.

competitors.name: Hero Bread
competitors.action: Hero Bread expanded its Crafted Collection with a personal-size pizza crust built around low-carb/high-protein macros: 4g net carbs, 20g protein, and 22g fiber per crust. The launch reframes pizza night around functional nutrition and at-home customization rather than a finished frozen pie, with DTC packs of four priced at $29.99.

competitors.name: Veggies Made Great
competitors.action: Veggies Made Great entered frozen breakfast pastry with Fruit Pockets, using butternut squash as the #1 crust ingredient and cauliflower-forward icing. The line is rolling into select Target, HyVee, Giant Food, The Giant Company, Stop & Shop, Wakefern, Harris Teeter and other accounts at a $5.99 suggested retail, signaling continued freezer-aisle demand for comfort formats with better-for-you ingredient stories.

trends.topic: Premium regional pizza styles are moving into frozen retail
trends.magnitude: Di Fara is taking a New York Grandma-style format into the freezer at $12.99 with second-half national expansion planned
trends.context: The frozen aisle is still rewarding brands that bring restaurant provenance and region-specific formats instead of competing only on mainstream round-pizza flavor line extensions.

trends.topic: Better-for-you pizza adjacencies are getting more macro-explicit
trends.magnitude: Hero's new crust leads with 4g net carbs, 20g protein, and 22g fiber per crust
trends.context: Pizza is increasingly being sold as a nutrition-managed meal platform, which matters for Real Dough if we ever test functional messaging or protein-forward variants.

breaking.headline: Today’s cleanest signal is that the frozen aisle keeps fragmenting into premium pizza provenance and functional-health positioning at the same time.
breaking.impact: Di Fara is proving there is still room to premiumize around regional pizza identity, while Hero and Veggies Made Great show how aggressively freezer brands are packaging comfort foods in better-for-you language. Real Dough should keep watching where premium craft cues and nutrition-forward messaging start overlapping.
